invoke_when: a workflow step needs a finished or draft visual or video ad asset, not just copy
steps: Read the concept brief and the format decision made in the workflow's format-economics step.
Match the format and source (brand-made, creator, catalogue, sequence) to one child skill using select_by.
Call the matching child skill and pass it the brief, references and claim tiers unchanged.
Return the child's output plus a one-line note naming which child ran and why.
checks: the correct child ran for the stated format and source
no format falls through with no child selected; an unmatched format stops and asks a person, it does not improvise
output: whatever the selected child skill outputs, plus a one-line routing note
skill_md:
---
name: make-creatives
owner: crea-paid-creative-copy
version: 1
invoke_when: a task needs a finished or draft ad asset, not just copy
inputs: concept brief, format decision, brand kit, claim tiers
outputs: routes to one child skill by format and source
---
Purpose: hold the one router every creative-build job passes through, so the agent
never guesses between two production paths and every build starts from the same
brief and claim-tier check.

Steps
1. Read the concept brief's stated format (static, video, catalogue, carousel) and
   source (brand-made, creator, synthetic actor).
2. Match to exactly one child: static, ugc-video, founder-video, catalogue-dpa or
   carousel, using the format and source fields together, never format alone,
   since a video could be UGC or founder-led.
3. Call the child with the brief, the tagged reference set and the claim tiers
   attached, unmodified.
4. If no child fits, for example a brand-new format not yet covered, stop and
   draft a one-page workflow proposal instead of forcing a near match.

Checks
- Every routed job names which child ran, in the handoff note.
- No build proceeds without a concept brief attached.
- A format with no matching child never gets forced into the nearest one.

Output: the child skill's exact output, plus a one-line routing note.

Example: brief says format=video, source=founder -> routes to
crea/make-creatives/founder-video, not ugc-video.

name: Static ad creative
invoke_when: the card's format is a still image ad for feed, story or search placements
steps: Choose the eye-path logic: clarity-first or curiosity-first, from the angle's awareness stage.
Pair the product image with the headline so the first glance states the benefit.
Set the primary-text weight (short punch versus a longer proof block) to match the placement.
Call the meta_gallery studio /api/variants endpoint with the reference and the real product photo, in product-accuracy mode.
Flag any localisation or catalogue/DPA note the design will need downstream.
Check the draft against the reference for layout and mood only, never copied text, logo, product or face.
checks: real product photo is used wherever fit, material or scale matters
no competitor logo, text, product or face appears in the draft
layout/mood credit for any reference is noted in the brief
output: static ad design brief plus one or more draft image variants, with the reference credit noted
skill_md:
---
name: make-creatives/static
owner: crea-paid-creative-copy
version: 1
invoke_when: format is static, a single image ad for feed, story or search
inputs: concept brief, reference image, real product photo, brand kit, headline/primary-text set
outputs: static design brief plus draft image variant(s)
---
Purpose: turn an approved concept into a design-ready static ad spec and a first
draft image, using the real product photo wherever accuracy matters and a
competitor reference for layout and mood only.

Steps
1. Pick clarity-first (state the benefit plainly) or curiosity-first (a visual
   hook that earns the read) from the angle's awareness stage: cold traffic
   usually needs curiosity, warm traffic usually needs clarity.
2. Pair the real product image with the headline so the pairing states one
   benefit at first glance, not two competing ideas.
3. Set primary-text weight for the placement: short and punchy for feed, longer
   proof-led text where the placement supports an expand.
4. Generate the draft through the creative studio's /api/variants call, passing
   the real product photo and the tagged reference image, with product-accuracy
   mode on so the product itself is never redrawn.
5. Note any localisation flag (script, currency, trust badge) or catalogue/DPA
   flag the design will need at scale.
6. Check the draft against the reference: same mood or layout only, nothing of
   the competitor's own text, logo, product or face reused.

Checks: real photo present where fit or scale matters; no competitor asset
copied; reference credit recorded.

Output: static design brief (eye path, pairing, text weight, CTA) plus the
draft image file(s) from the studio.

Example: a cold-traffic protein-bar ad pairs a macro shot of the bar breaking
open with a curiosity headline ("the bar that doesn't taste like a bar"),
studio-generated with the real product photo, credited to one tagged
competitor reference for its close-up crop style only.

name: UGC video creative
invoke_when: the card's format is video and the source is a creator or a real customer, not the brand itself
steps: Decide the UGC source: a briefed creator, a whitelisted organic post, or an AI-actor stand-in (route to ai-actor-ugc if synthetic).
For a briefed creator, pick a wide (discovery) or specific (replication) brief and write the concept, do/don't list and take allowance.
For an organic post, confirm it already passed the organic-ugc-scout vetting bar and rights are logged.
Set the usage-rights scope and expiry before any paid use.
Check the finished or incoming clip against the angle brief for message match.
Log the source, rights and concept to the registry.
checks: never a UGC brief with no concept, only 'make content'
rights scope and expiry are logged before paid use
the clip's claim matches the audited angle, no drift from what the creator improvised
output: creator or sourcing brief (for a briefed/organic path) or a routing note to ai-actor-ugc, plus the rights log entry
skill_md:

name: make-creatives/ugc-video
owner: crea-paid-creative-copy
version: 1
invoke_when: format is video and the source is a creator or real customer, not the brand
inputs: avatar, objection map, Scout references, claim tiers, creator roster or organic shortlist
outputs: creator or sourcing brief, rights log entry, or a route to the synthetic path
---
Purpose: get a genuine, rights-cleared UGC-style video into production, from
whichever real source fits the concept, without ever sending a creator to "make
content" with no concept.

Steps
1. Decide the source: a creator to brief fresh, an already-scouted organic post
   to license, or (only when the founder wants a fast test with no real creator)
   a synthetic AI-actor stand-in, which routes to make-creatives/ai-actor-ugc
   instead of this skill's own path.
2. For a fresh creator, pick a wide brief (let them discover the angle) or a
   specific brief (replicate a proven structure), then write the concept, a
   do/don't list and the number of takes allowed.
3. For an organic post, confirm it cleared the organic-ugc-scout vetting bar
   (authenticity, product visibility, tone) before treating it as usable.
4. Set the rights scope, paid whitelisting or organic-only, and the expiry date,
   before any spend touches the content.
5. Check the delivered or sourced clip against the angle brief: does it argue
   the same claim, or did the creator drift.
6. Log source, concept and rights to the registry.

Checks: concept present, not just an instruction; rights logged before paid use;
message match to the angle.

Output: creator brief or organic-sourcing note, with rights terms attached.

Example: angle is "finally, a stroller that fits the trunk"; brief asks a parent
creator to film their real trunk before and after, specific brief, 2 takes,
paid-whitelist rights for 6 months.

name: Founder-led video creative
invoke_when: the card's format is video and the source is the founder or another named authority figure
steps: Confirm the founder's real, permissioned facts and reviews are on file, never invented.
Frame the video as an argument for the viewer's problem: claim, proof, mechanism, never a biography.
Write the scene-by-scene script in the proven order: hook, bridge, mechanism, product, proof, objection, CTA.
Diversify delivery: vary setting, proof point and framing across 2 to 3 variants so it never reads as the same clip repeated.
Set shot direction that keeps the founder's real likeness and the product accurate.
Run the claim and copywriting pass before it leaves this skill.
checks: no invented founder story or credential
single CTA per script
founder's real face and product are never redrawn
output: founder fact sheet, script variants, and a shot list or frame-direction note
skill_md:
---
name: make-creatives/founder-video
owner: crea-paid-creative-copy
version: 1
invoke_when: format is video and the source is the founder or a named authority
inputs: founder fact sheet, angle brief, claim tiers, existing hook bank
outputs: script variants, shot or frame-direction note
---
Purpose: script and direct a founder or authority-led ad as a real argument for
the viewer's problem, never a life-story reel, using only real, permissioned
facts.

Steps
1. Pull the founder's or authority's real stories, credentials and reviews from
   the brand brain, with a source and date for each; nothing invented, and stop
   if a strong story has no written permission on file.
2. Frame the video as claim, proof, mechanism, stating the viewer's problem in
   the first line, not the founder's history.
3. Script scene by scene in the proven order: hook, bridge, mechanism, product,
   proof, objection, CTA, sized to how much the product actually needs to be
   explained.
4. Draft 2 to 3 variants that vary setting, delivery style and the specific
   proof point used, so repeated founder appearances do not read as one ad
   recycled.
5. Set shot direction: gaze toward the CTA, the real product visible and
   accurate, no AI redraw of the founder's face or the product itself.
6. Run the copywriting and claim-tier pass on every spoken and on-screen line
   before handoff.

Checks: no invented fact; single CTA; no redrawn face or product.

Output: script variants (scene, visual, line, purpose) plus a shot list.

Example: founder explains why a formula works using a real customer's return
review as proof, three variants swap the review quoted but keep the same claim
and mechanism.

name: Catalogue and DPA creative
invoke_when: the card is a catalogue or dynamic product ad (DPA) campaign covering many SKUs from the product feed, or a feed schema change
inputs_required: product feed: price, image, SKU fields
steps: Audit the feed for gaps, malformed fields or stale data before building anything on top of it.
Design the overlay template (price, discount, badge) tested against the longest price string and smallest image in the feed.
Generate the full variant grid by combining the template, the feed fields and the copy blocks.
Spot-check a random sample of SKUs for correct price, image and copy pairing.
Flag SKU-level risk: overlapping badge, missing image, a discontinued item still live.
checks: template tested against real longest/shortest feed values, not a sample assumption
every flagged risk names the specific SKU, not a generalized warning
output: overlay template, catalogue-scale variant grid, SKU-level risk flag list
skill_md:
---
name: make-creatives/catalogue-dpa
owner: crea-paid-creative-copy
version: 1
invoke_when: the job covers many SKUs from the product feed: a new catalogue or
  DPA campaign, or a feed schema change
inputs: product feed, brand kit, reusable copy block set
outputs: overlay template, full variant grid, SKU-level risk flags
---
Purpose: build a price and badge overlay template and generate the full
catalogue-scale ad grid, since these follow a fixed module system unlike a
one-off static, and a template that fails on one SKU fails silently at scale.

Steps
1. Audit the feed's price and image fields for gaps, wrong formats or stale
   data first; building a template on dirty data hides the real problem.
2. Design the overlay: price, discount badge, any urgency badge, tested against
   the single longest real price string in the feed and the smallest real
   product image, not an average case.
3. Write or reuse a small set of copy blocks that plug into any SKU's fields
   without reading oddly for an outlier product name or price.
4. Generate the variant grid by combining template, feed fields and copy
   blocks through the creative studio's variant endpoint.
5. Spot-check a random sample, not just the first few SKUs, for correct price,
   image and copy pairing.
6. Flag every SKU-specific risk by name: a badge overlapping a long price, a
   missing image, a discontinued SKU still marked active.

Checks: template survives the extreme cases in the feed; every risk names a
SKU, not a category.

Output: overlay template file, the generated variant grid, and a risk list.

Example: a Black-Friday-sale badge overlaps a 6-digit price on 4 SKUs out of
800; the audit catches it before the DPA campaign goes live, not after.

name: Carousel ad creative
invoke_when: the card's format is a multi-card carousel that tells a sequence: steps, a range, or a before-to-after story
steps: Confirm the format-economics step actually favors a sequence over a single image or video.
Pick the sequence logic: step-by-step use, a size or variant range, or a before-to-after story.
Write one headline per card so each card earns the swipe to the next.
Pair each card's image with its own headline, real product photos throughout.
Set the final card as the offer and CTA card, never buried mid-sequence.
Check the full sequence reads correctly even if a viewer only sees the first 2 cards.
checks: sequence has a clear reason to be a carousel, not a single static forced into cards
final card carries the offer and CTA
first 2 cards alone still make sense and earn a swipe
output: carousel card sequence: ordered image-headline pairs plus the CTA card
skill_md:
---
name: make-creatives/carousel
owner: crea-paid-creative-copy
version: 1
invoke_when: format is a multi-card carousel telling a sequence, not a single
  static or video
inputs: concept brief, format-economics decision, product facts, headline/primary-text set
outputs: ordered carousel card sequence with a CTA card
---
Purpose: build a carousel that earns each swipe, using a real sequence logic,
rather than defaulting to cards just because the format exists.

Steps
1. Check that format-economics actually chose carousel because the product has
   a real sequence to show: steps of use, a size or variant range, or a
   before-to-after story. If not, send it back to static or video instead.
2. Pick the sequence logic explicitly and state it in the brief, so every card
   is built to advance that one logic, not a grab-bag of images.
3. Write one headline per card that earns the next swipe on its own, testing
   the first 2 cards as if that is all a viewer will ever see.
4. Pair each card's real product image with its headline; no card runs on a
   generic stock image with no connection to the sequence.
5. Put the offer and CTA on the final card, not mid-sequence where it gets
   skipped.
6. Read the full sequence end to end for message-match and pacing before
   handoff.

Checks: real sequence logic named; first 2 cards stand alone; CTA on the last
card.

Output: an ordered list of image-headline card pairs plus the CTA card, tagged
with the sequence logic used.

Example: a skincare routine ad uses 4 cards, one per step, ending on card 5
with the bundle price and a single CTA, rather than 5 unrelated product shots.

name: Write ad copy
invoke_when: a workflow step needs copy text, not a visual or video build
steps: Read what copy type the step needs.
Match to one child skill by copy_type using select_by.
Call the child with the angle brief, product facts and claim tiers attached.
Return the child's output plus which child ran.
checks: the correct child ran for the stated copy type
no copy leaves this skill without the claim-tier check downstream
output: the selected child's exact output, plus a routing note

owner: crea-paid-creative-copy
version: 1
invoke_when: a task needs written copy, not a visual or video build
inputs: angle brief, product facts, claim tiers, platform character limits
outputs: routes to one child skill by copy_type
---
Purpose: hold the one router every copywriting job passes through, so a hook
request never lands on the headline child by mistake and every draft carries
the same brand facts.

Steps
1. Read the copy_type the step names: primary text, headline, hook, or a
   full script.
2. Route to exactly one child. A cold-open video needs both hooks and scripts:
   call hooks first, then feed the winning hook into scripts.
3. Pass the angle brief, product facts and claim tiers to the child unchanged.
4. Return the child's output with a one-line note on which child ran, so the
   downstream compliance step knows which checklist applies.

Checks
- The right child ran for the stated copy_type.
- No copy is treated as finished before the compliance pass (a separate step in
  every workflow) runs on it.
- A copy_type with no matching child stops and asks a person rather than
  forcing a near match.

Output: the child skill's exact output plus a one-line routing note.

Example: task says copy_type=hook, format=video -> routes to
crea/write-copy/hooks; the winning hook then feeds crea/write-copy/scripts.

name: Primary text and body copy
invoke_when: the copy needed is the main body text under a static, carousel card, or marketplace module, not a headline or a spoken script
steps: State the one dominant appeal in the opening line.
Build the proof point or mechanism in the middle, ranked by strongest evidence first.
Close on the offer and a single CTA.
Fit the exact character or space limit for the placement (feed, carousel card, marketplace module).
Check reading level and single-idea discipline before returning.
checks: opening line states the appeal, not a generic greeting
one CTA only
fits the placement's real space limit
output: primary text block, sized to the placement, with a reading-level score
skill_md:
---
name: write-copy/primary-text
owner: crea-paid-creative-copy
version: 1
invoke_when: the copy needed is body text under a static, carousel card or
  marketplace module, not a headline or spoken script
inputs: angle brief, cleared claim list, platform character/space limit
outputs: primary text block with a reading-level score
---
Purpose: write body copy that opens on the dominant appeal, proves it in order
of evidence strength, and closes on one clear action, fit to the exact space
the placement gives it.

Steps
1. Open on the angle's one dominant appeal, stated as a specific outcome, never
   a generic greeting or a restated headline.
2. Order proof points from strongest real evidence (a number, a named review,
   a demonstrable mechanism) to weakest, cutting anything with no evidence
   behind it.
3. Close on the offer stated plainly and exactly one CTA; a second competing
   CTA is cut, not softened.
4. Fit the text to the placement's real limit: a feed ad tolerates a short
   punch, a carousel card needs far less, a marketplace module has its own
   fixed character cap.
5. Score reading level in code and cut or simplify until it clears grade 10.

Checks: one dominant appeal, one CTA, no claim outside the cleared list, fits
the real space limit, reading level under grade 10.

Output: the finished primary text string, its word and character count, and
its reading-grade score.

Example: a mattress ad's primary text opens "sleep hot? this one breathes,"
then cites the one clinical measurement on file, then closes with "try it 100
nights, free returns" and a single Shop Now CTA.

name: Headline sets
invoke_when: the copy needed is the short headline line above or beside the image, for statics, search or marketplace listings
inputs_required: reference image if pairing a static
steps: Draft 10 or more headline candidates from the angle's dominant appeal, varying the specific benefit stated.
Check each candidate against the reference image for pairing fit, not a mismatched claim.
Check each candidate's length against the platform's current character limit.
Rank the set and mark the top 3 to 5 as the primary test set.
checks: 10+ candidates drafted before any get cut
every kept headline fits the current character limit
no headline states a claim the paired image contradicts
output: ranked headline set (10+ candidates, top 3-5 marked), each with its character count
skill_md:
---
name: write-copy/headlines
owner: crea-paid-creative-copy
version: 1
invoke_when: the copy needed is a short headline for a static, search or
  marketplace listing
inputs: angle brief, cleared claim list, reference image if pairing a static,
  platform character limit
outputs: ranked headline set with character counts
---
Purpose: produce a real range of headline candidates, not three near-identical
rewordings, and confirm each one fits both its space limit and the image it
runs beside.

Steps
1. Draft 10 or more candidates from the angle's dominant appeal, varying the
   specific benefit named (speed, price, comfort, status) rather than just
   rewording one phrase 10 times.
2. Where a static image is already chosen, check each candidate against it:
   the headline and the image should state one shared idea, not two competing
   claims.
3. Check every candidate's character count against the platform's current
   limit; cut or shorten anything that would truncate.
4. Rank the full set and mark the top 3 to 5 as the ones to actually test,
   with a one-line reason for the ranking.

Checks: 10+ candidates before culling; no length violation; no image-headline
mismatch; ranking reasoned, not arbitrary.

Output: the full candidate list, each with its character count, and the top
3-5 flagged for test.

Example: for a cold-brew concentrate, candidates range across speed ("coffee
in 10 seconds"), price ("75 cents a cup") and taste ("less bitter, more
buzz"), ranked by which best pairs with the chosen close-up product shot.

name: Hook bank
invoke_when: the copy needed is the opening line or opening 3 seconds of a cold video, VSL or static, before any full script is written
steps: Draft 8 to 20 hooks covering different opening mechanisms (question, bold claim, pattern interrupt, relatable scene).
Grade each hook on 5 criteria: clarity, relevance, novelty, specificity, credibility.
Multiply the top-graded hook into layered variants across audio, on-screen text and visual, for video formats.
Confirm no hook names the product or the offer, since a cold hook should earn attention before either.
Rank the bank and flag the top 3 to 5 for test.
checks: 8 to 20 hooks drafted before grading
no product name or offer in a cold hook
top hooks flagged with a grading reason
output: graded hook bank (8-20 hooks, each with 5 scores), top 3-5 flagged, with audio/text/visual variants for video
skill_md:
---
name: write-copy/hooks
owner: crea-paid-creative-copy
version: 1
invoke_when: the copy needed is an opening line, before hook rate, for cold
  video, VSL or static formats
inputs: angle brief, past hook grades, product facts
outputs: graded hook bank with variants
---
Purpose: produce and grade enough real hook variety that a genuinely strong
opening survives the cut, rather than shipping the first idea that came to
mind.

Steps
1. Draft 8 to 20 hooks spanning different opening mechanisms: a direct
   question, a bold or surprising claim, a pattern interrupt (visual or
   verbal), and a relatable scene the viewer recognizes.
2. Grade every hook on 5 criteria: clarity (understood in one read), relevance
   (matches the persona's real problem), novelty (not the account's own
   overused opener), specificity (a real detail, not a vague promise) and
   credibility (believable without proof yet shown).
3. For video, take the top-graded hook and build layered variants: a different
   audio delivery, a different on-screen text treatment, a different opening
   visual, so one strong idea gets 3 or 4 real chances to test.
4. Check that no hook names the product or the offer; a cold hook earns the
   next 3 seconds first.
5. Rank the full bank and flag the top 3 to 5 with the reason they ranked
   there.

Checks: 8-20 hooks before grading; every hook scored on all 5 criteria; no
premature product/offer name.

Output: the graded bank, angle-tagged, format-tagged, with the top hooks
flagged and video variants attached.

Example: for a scalp-serum brand, hooks span "why does my scalp itch by
noon?" (question), "your shampoo is the problem" (bold claim) and a silent
close-up of flaking that cuts before a word is said (pattern interrupt).

name: Video scripts and storyboards
invoke_when: the copy needed is a full scene-by-scene video script, for cold video, VSL, testimonial-style or synthetic-actor reads
steps: Decide if a full VSL is warranted or a short cold-video structure fits better, from the product's real education need.
Pick the skeleton: 7-part VSL, cold-video 7-beat (hook, bridge, mechanism, product, proof, objection, CTA), or testimonial structure.
Draft scene by scene: time, visual, on-screen text, voice line, purpose.
Storyboard the shot list sized to how it will actually be shot or generated.
Check claim-proof pairing: every claim in the script has its proof beat nearby.
Confirm a single CTA closes the script.
checks: CTA present and singular
no unverified claim
claim and its proof sit close together in the sequence
output: scene-by-scene script table plus storyboard shot list
skill_md:
---
name: write-copy/scripts
owner: crea-paid-creative-copy
version: 1
invoke_when: the copy needed is a full video script, cold video, VSL,
  testimonial-style, or a synthetic-actor read
inputs: angle brief, hook bank, claim tiers, the product's real education need
outputs: scene-by-scene script table plus storyboard shot list
---
Purpose: script video ads in a proven, sized structure, never longer than the
product's real education need justifies, with every claim paired to its proof.

Steps
1. Decide the format length from the product's real complexity: a simple
   impulse product rarely needs a full VSL; a high-consideration or
   unfamiliar-mechanism product often does.
2. Pick the skeleton: the 7-part VSL for longer education, the cold-video
   7-beat (hook, bridge, mechanism, product, proof, objection, CTA) for
   shorter formats, or a testimonial structure built around a real customer
   story.
3. Write scene by scene as a table: timestamp, what's on screen, any on-screen
   text, the spoken line, and that beat's purpose in the argument.
4. Storyboard the shot list, sized to whether this will be a real shoot, a
   creator's own filming, or an AI-actor generation, since each needs a
   different level of shot detail.
5. Check claim-proof pairing: every claim made has its proof beat within a
   few seconds, not deferred to the end.
6. Confirm exactly one CTA closes the script.

Checks: single CTA; no unpaired claim; length matches the real education need,
not a habit.

Output: the scene table and the storyboard, both tagged to the angle and
format they serve.

Example: a water-filter VSL spends 20 seconds on the contamination problem,
15 on the mechanism with a visual proof, 10 on a real lab result, then closes
on price and one CTA, rather than padding to a fixed runtime.

name: Objection and format scan
invoke_when: a new test needs its research pulled fresh before angles can be written
inputs_required: own account's last 90 days of ad-level results
steps: Pull the brand's already-mined voice-of-customer packet (owned by the Brand Brain Keeper).
Pull the account's own last 90 days of ad-level results and rank formats by hook rate, hold rate and CPA.
Tag every objection to its real quoted source and date.
Tag every 'format working now' line to the real metric behind it.
Flag anything that reads as a surprise rather than a confirmation of known research.
checks: every objection has a quoted source and date
every format claim cites a real metric, not an impression
output: objection map (quoted, sourced) plus a format scan (metric-backed)
skill_md:
---
name: research/objection-and-format-scan
owner: crea-paid-creative-copy
version: 1
invoke_when: a new creative test needs its research refreshed before angles get
  written
inputs: brand brain voice-of-customer packet, own account's last 90 days of
  ad-level results
outputs: sourced objection map, metric-backed format scan
---
Purpose: assemble the research a new angle needs, using the brand's own
already-mined customer language and this account's own real recent results,
rather than a generic best-practice list.

Steps
1. Pull the current voice-of-customer packet from the brand brain, which the
   Brand Brain Keeper owns and refreshes; this skill does not re-mine raw
   customer data itself, it assembles what already exists for this decision.
2. Pull this account's own last 90 days of ad-level results and rank which
   formats currently deliver the best hook rate, hold rate and CPA, since
   "what's working now" should mean this account, not the category in
   general.
3. Tag every objection carried into the map with its real quoted source and a
   date, never a paraphrase presented as a quote.
4. Tag every format claim to the specific metric and window that backs it.
5. Flag anything in the pull that reads as a genuine surprise rather than a
   confirmation of what the team already believed, since surprises are where
   a new angle usually hides.

Checks: source and date on every objection; metric and window on every format
claim.

Output: the objection map and the format scan, both ready to feed the
angle-builder skill.

Example: the scan shows static ads with a price-anchor angle now outperform
video 2-to-1 on CPA over the last 90 days, a fact the format-economics step
later uses directly.

name: Competitor signal pull
invoke_when: a workflow step needs layout or mood references from competitor ads, never their text, logo, product or face
steps: Pull competitor ads from the gallery's Competitors tab matching the bottleneck or persona.
Call the Reference Scout for any additional swipe material outside the gallery's own set.
Tag each reference with one line on why it fits.
Mark every reference layout/mood only, never for text, logo, product or face reuse.
Cap the set at 3 to 8 references so the brief stays usable.
checks: every reference has a one-line fit reason
every reference is explicitly tagged signal only
output: 3 to 8 tagged competitor references, layout/mood only
skill_md:
---
name: research/competitor-signal-pull
owner: crea-paid-creative-copy
version: 1
invoke_when: a step needs competitor references for layout or mood, never for
  copying text, logo, product or face
inputs: objection map or bottleneck, comp_media.json, competitors.json
outputs: 3 to 8 tagged, layout/mood-only references
---
Purpose: gather real competitor structure signal, cadence, layout and mood,
without ever crossing into using a competitor's actual text, logo, product or
face, and without treating any of it as a proven winner.

Steps
1. Pull competitor ads from the Meta gallery's Competitors tab that match the
   current bottleneck or persona, using the existing tagged competitor data
   (competitors.json, comp_media.json) rather than a fresh scrape.
2. Where the gallery's own set does not have enough range, call the Reference
   Scout for additional swipe material under the same layout/mood-only rule.
3. Write a one-line reason each reference was pulled: what structural or mood
   element it demonstrates, never "because it looks good."
4. Mark every single reference as signal only, explicitly, in the handoff, so
   a downstream skill cannot mistake it for cleared source material.
5. Cap the final set at 3 to 8 references; more than that stops being usable
   in a brief.

Checks: every reference has a fit reason; every reference is tagged signal
only; no reference implies a proven result.

Output: the tagged reference set, ready to attach to a concept or design
brief.

Example: 5 competitor statics are pulled for their shared "before/after split
screen" layout on a skincare bottleneck, none of their headlines or product
shots are carried forward.

name: Angle builder
invoke_when: a research packet exists and a small set of testable angles needs to be defined before any copy is written
steps: Write the one-sentence angle for one persona.
State the buying question the angle answers.
Pick the single dominant appeal (price, status, ease, fear-avoidance, aspiration).
Set the awareness stage the angle targets.
Check the angle against claim tiers before it leaves this skill.
Repeat to produce 2 to 4 distinct angle candidates.
checks: each angle names one persona, one appeal, one buying question
no forbidden-tier claim in any angle
output: angle brief: 2 to 4 angles, each with persona, appeal, buying question, awareness stage
skill_md:
---
name: angle-and-test/angle-builder
owner: crea-paid-creative-copy
version: 1
invoke_when: research exists and a small set of testable angles must be
  defined before any copy gets written
inputs: objection map, persona/avatar record, product facts, claim tiers
outputs: 2 to 4 angle candidates, each fully specified
---
Purpose: turn raw research into a small, genuinely distinct set of testable
angles, each disciplined to one persona and one dominant appeal, so a test
batch actually isolates what it claims to test.

Steps
1. Write the angle as one sentence for one named persona; an angle that tries
   to speak to two personas at once gets split into two angles instead.
2. State the exact buying question the angle answers, in the persona's own
   words where the research supports it.
3. Pick a single dominant appeal, price, status, ease, fear-avoidance or
   aspiration, and hold to it; an angle mixing two appeals is not one testable
   thing.
4. Set the awareness stage (unaware, problem-aware, solution-aware,
   product-aware, most-aware) the angle is built for, since the hook, proof
   and CTA all depend on it.
5. Check the angle against the brand's claim tiers immediately, before any
   copy is written on top of it, so a bad angle is caught at its cheapest
   point.
6. Produce 2 to 4 distinct candidates this way, not near-duplicates of one
   idea.

Checks: one persona, one appeal, one buying question per angle; no
forbidden-tier claim.

Output: the angle brief, each candidate fully specified and ready for the
test-plan-builder or a founder-video argument outline.

Example: from an objection map full of "will this actually fit my small
kitchen," one angle targets space-anxious apartment cooks on the ease appeal,
answering "does this take up counter space I don't have."

name: Test plan builder
invoke_when: an angle brief is ready and the creative side of a test needs a hypothesis, pack size and pre-set win/kill rule
inputs_required: registry: past test sizes for this brand
steps: Write the hypothesis in one sentence: what changes, and what it should move.
Set a clean one-persona-per-ad-set structure so the test isolates the angle.
Size the pack from this account's own delivery volume, not a fixed generic number.
Set the winner rule and the kill rule before any script is written.
Set the minimum read window from the account's own delivery, not a calendar default.
checks: winner and kill rule exist before launch
pack size and read window both derive from this account's real traffic
output: test brief: hypothesis, pack size, winner rule, kill rule, minimum read window
skill_md:
---
name: angle-and-test/test-plan-builder
owner: crea-paid-creative-copy
version: 1
invoke_when: an angle brief is ready and the creative side of a test needs a
  hypothesis and a pre-set win/kill rule
inputs: angle brief, metric contract delivery volume, registry of past test
  sizes for this brand
outputs: test brief with hypothesis, pack size, winner/kill rule, read window
---
Purpose: fix the test's judgment criteria before a single script is written,
so no one is tempted to move the goalposts once real numbers start coming in;
covers the creative side of the test only; MEDIA owns the budget and delivery
mechanics of the same test.

Steps
1. Write the hypothesis as one sentence: which angle or hook change is being
   tested, and which specific metric it should move (hook rate, CVR, CPA).
2. Structure the test as one persona per ad set, so a result can be
   attributed to the angle, not blurred across personas sharing a set.
3. Size the pack, how many ad variants launch at once, from this account's
   own real delivery volume using metric-read, not a fixed "always test 5"
   rule; a low-volume account needs a smaller, cleaner pack.
4. Set the winner rule and the kill rule in the same sentence as the
   hypothesis, before any creative exists, so the eventual read has no room
   for a post-hoc rationalization.
5. Set the minimum read window from the account's own delivery, enough days
   to reach a meaningful sample, not a calendar habit like "always 7 days."

Checks: rules exist before scripting starts; every number in the plan is
computed from real account data, not a template default.

Output: the test brief, handed whole into the launch checklist step.

Example: hypothesis "the price-anchor angle beats the durability angle on
CPA"; pack of 4 (2 per angle) sized to the account's 40-purchase/week volume;
winner rule is CPA 20% below target at 50+ purchases per ad.

name: Audience spec handoff
invoke_when: an angle's persona needs to become a concrete targeting spec and be handed to the Media buyer, without CREA building or launching it
steps: Pull the persona's real traits: age range, interests, in-group language, past-attempt behaviors.
Translate each trait into a targetable field (age range, interest, behavior, lookalike seed).
Set exclusions: existing customers, brand-term searchers, any persona this angle should not reach.
Package the spec with the persona id and angle id attached.
Hand the spec to MEDIA as a structured request; do not build or launch an audience.
checks: every targeting trait ties to a line in the persona record, not a guess
exclusions are explicit, not assumed
output: audience spec record: age range, traits, exclusions, matched persona id, handed to MEDIA
skill_md:
---
name: angle-and-test/audience-spec-handoff
owner: crea-paid-creative-copy
version: 1
invoke_when: an angle's persona needs to become a concrete targeting spec for
  MEDIA, without CREA touching the ad account
inputs: angle brief, persona/avatar record, past audience performance
outputs: audience spec record handed to MEDIA
---
Purpose: translate a persona into age, traits and exclusions a media buyer can
act on, while keeping account-building and launch strictly on MEDIA's side of
the line.

Steps
1. Pull the persona's real, research-grounded traits: age range, stated
   interests, in-group language, and what they say they already tried and
   rejected.
2. Translate each trait into a field a targeting spec actually uses: an age
   range, an interest or behavior category, or a lookalike seed source; a
   trait that cannot translate honestly is left out rather than forced.
3. Set exclusions explicitly: current customers who should not see a cold
   angle, brand-term searchers, and any persona this specific angle would
   alienate.
4. Package the spec with the source persona id and the angle id so MEDIA can
   trace it back to the research behind it.
5. Hand the spec to MEDIA as a structured request and stop; CREA never opens
   an ads-manager targeting screen itself.

Checks: every trait traces to the persona record; exclusions stated, not
assumed; handoff is a request, not an action.

Output: the audience spec record, logged and sent to MEDIA.

Example: persona "budget-anxious new parent, 24-34" becomes age 24-34,
interest tags for baby-gear comparison content, lookalike seed from past
90-day purchasers, exclusion on existing customers and brand-term searchers.

name: Format economics comparison
invoke_when: a concept is set and the ad format still needs choosing, compared by expected profit per ad rather than ROAS alone
inputs_required: account's own cost-per-asset and format hit-rate history
steps: List the candidate formats the concept could run as.
Pull this account's own cost-per-asset and hit-rate by format.
Compute expected profit per ad per format: (hit rate x average result value) minus cost per asset.
Weigh the product's real education or demo need against the fastest-to-produce format.
State the decision with the number behind it.
checks: decision cites a computed number, not a stated preference
product's real education need is checked, not assumed satisfied by any format
output: format decision with the profit-per-ad comparison shown
skill_md:
---
name: angle-and-test/format-economics
owner: crea-paid-creative-copy
version: 1
invoke_when: a concept is set and the format still needs choosing, compared
  by real economics, not habit or ROAS alone
inputs: angle brief, test brief, product's education/demo need, account's own
  cost-per-asset and format hit-rate history
outputs: format decision with the comparison shown
---
Purpose: pick the ad format from this account's own numbers, since a format
with a lower hit rate but a much lower cost per asset can beat a flashier,
expensive format on real profit per ad.

Steps
1. List every format the concept could reasonably run as: static, native
   platform format, UGC video, founder video, carousel, catalogue.
2. Pull this account's own cost-per-asset and win-rate history by format,
   using metric-read; a brand-new account with no history falls back to the
   product's education need alone, stated as such.
3. Compute expected profit per ad for each candidate format: hit rate times
   the average result value of a winning ad in that format, minus the real
   cost to produce one asset in that format.
4. Weigh this against the product's real education or demonstration need; a
   product that needs to be seen in motion should not default to static just
   because static is cheaper, if the computed profit favors video anyway.
5. State the final decision with the actual numbers shown, not a preference
   dressed as a conclusion.

Checks: decision has a number behind it; product's real demo need was
checked explicitly, not skipped.

Output: the format decision plus the profit-per-ad table that produced it.

Example: static costs 1/5th of a UGC video to produce and hits 22% of the
time versus 30% for UGC; on this account's numbers static still wins on
profit per ad because the cost gap outweighs the hit-rate gap.

name: Concept brief builder
invoke_when: an idea is approved and the fixed one-page brief must exist before any design tool or shoot is booked
steps: Fill every fixed field: persona, angle, offer, destination, format, awareness stage.
Confirm the destination link actually matches the offer stated.
Confirm hook, image and copy plan all share one awareness stage.
Attach the reference set and claim sources used.
Return the finished brief, no blank fields.
checks: no field left blank
destination link matches the offer stated
one shared awareness stage across hook/image/copy
output: one-page concept brief document
skill_md:
---
name: briefing/concept-brief
owner: crea-paid-creative-copy
version: 1
invoke_when: an idea is approved and the fixed brief must exist before any
  design tool or shoot is booked
inputs: approved idea record, angle brief, product facts
outputs: one-page concept brief, every field filled
---
Purpose: produce the same fixed-field brief every time, so a designer, video
editor or creator always gets the same shape of instruction regardless of
which angle or format is behind it.

Steps
1. Fill every fixed field in order: persona, angle (one sentence), dominant
   appeal, buying question, offer, destination, format, awareness stage.
2. Confirm the destination link actually sells the offer stated in the brief;
   a brief promising a bundle that the linked page does not show is sent back,
   not shipped with a note.
3. Confirm the hook, the planned image or video direction, and the copy plan
   all target the same awareness stage; a cold hook paired with a
   product-aware landing page is a mismatch caught here, not after launch.
4. Attach the reference set used (layout/mood only) and the claim sources
   behind any stated benefit.
5. Return the brief only once every field is filled; a blank field is treated
   as a stop, not a placeholder to fill in later.

Checks: no blank field; destination matches offer; one shared awareness
stage.

Output: the concept brief document, ready to feed the format-specific
production brief.

Example: brief for the "price-anchor" angle states destination as the
bundle page, not the single-unit page, since the offer field says "3-pack
bundle discount."

name: Native platform format craft
invoke_when: the chosen platform is TikTok- or Reels-style and the concept must be written so it does not read as a paid ad
inputs_required: product's actual real trait to feature
steps: Pick a native format from the product's real trait, not a passing trend.
Write it in the platform's own editorial voice, pacing and on-screen text conventions.
Avoid a polished, brand-commercial look that breaks the platform's own feed pattern.
Check the format still carries the angle's claim and CTA, even inside a native structure.
checks: format picked from a real product trait, not copied from a trending format with no fit
claim and CTA survive inside the native structure
output: native-format concept and script/shot notes
skill_md:
---
name: briefing/native-format-craft
owner: crea-paid-creative-copy
version: 1
invoke_when: the platform is TikTok- or Reels-style and the ad must not read
  as an ad
inputs: angle brief, the product's real feature-worthy trait, current
  platform editorial conventions
outputs: native-format concept with script or shot notes
---
Purpose: fit the concept into how the platform's own users actually post,
picked from something real about the product, not a trend with no connection
to it.

Steps
1. Pick the native format (a POV, a "get ready with me," a quick-tip list, a
   duet-style reaction) from a real, specific trait of the product, for
   example a satisfying unboxing motion or a genuinely surprising use case,
   never a trending format bolted on with no fit.
2. Write in the platform's own pacing: shorter beats, native captions style,
   the on-screen text conventions real creators use, not a repurposed TV-ad
   script.
3. Deliberately avoid the polished, brand-commercial look; a rougher, native
   feel is the point, since it is what keeps the ad from breaking the
   feed's own pattern.
4. Check the angle's claim and the CTA still survive inside the native
   structure; native does not mean the ad forgets to sell.

Checks: format ties to a real product trait; claim and CTA present despite
the native wrapper.

Output: the native-format concept plus script or shot notes in the
platform's own voice.

Example: a phone-case brand's "drop test" becomes a native-feeling POV of
someone actually dropping their phone on tile, not a studio slow-motion ad.

name: Shoot and photo direction
invoke_when: a real product shoot is being run, or any AI-touched image needs direction so the product shown matches what ships
inputs_required: product facts: real dimensions, material, color, fit
steps: Set image-accuracy direction naming the exact product variant or SKU being shot.
Build the numbered shot list with angles and gaze direction toward the CTA.
Book studio/location/model within the approved production budget.
Get signed model and location releases before the shoot starts.
QA retouching or AI-touch against the real product for color, fit, scale and material.
File and version the checked frames.
checks: release on file before use
no retouch or AI-touch changes a fact-bearing detail
output: image-accuracy brief, shot list, QA'd final frame set
skill_md:
---
name: briefing/shoot-and-photo-direction
owner: crea-paid-creative-copy
version: 1
invoke_when: a real shoot is running, or any AI-touched image needs direction
  so the product shown matches what a customer actually receives
inputs: concept or founder brief, real product facts (dimensions, material,
  color, fit)
outputs: image-accuracy brief, shot list, QA'd final frame set
---
Purpose: keep every photographed or AI-touched product image honest to what
ships, since a mismatch here becomes a return, a bad review or a platform
complaint, not just a design nitpick.

Steps
1. Set direction naming the exact product variant or SKU being shot; a
   generic "the product" instruction invites the wrong color or size on set.
2. Build a numbered shot list tied to a specific ad or page use, with the
   subject's gaze pointed toward the CTA whenever a person is in frame.
3. Book the studio, location and any model within the approved production
   budget from the current monthly plan.
4. Collect signed model and location releases before the shoot starts, never
   retroactively.
5. Check every retouched or AI-touched frame against the real product facts:
   color must match, scale must read correctly next to a known object,
   material texture must still look like the real material, not a stylized
   redraw.
6. File and version the checked frames under the naming standard before
   they are usable downstream.

Checks: release on file before use; no fact-bearing detail altered by
retouching or AI.

Output: the image-accuracy brief, the shot list, and the QA'd final frames.

Example: a rug brand's AI background swap is allowed to change the room
scene, never the rug's actual weave pattern or true color under warm light.

name: Localisation spec
invoke_when: creative or copy needs specifying for a target market and device with its own payment, delivery and language norms
steps: Confirm device target: standard feed and story formats by default, or mobile-first, vertical-only formats where the target market's traffic calls for it.

Pull the market's real trust facts: payment method mix (card, wallets, BNPL for a US brand), delivery windows, local payment logos; COD availability and EMI where the target market runs them (markets: IN).
Note the language pair and whether a dual-language, code-switched line is needed.
Flag any mismatched trust line inherited from another market that must be swapped out.
Set the market tag every downstream asset must carry.
checks: every trust fact matches current brand policy for that market, not an assumption
device target stated explicitly
output: target spec sheet: device target, market trust facts, language notes, market tag
skill_md:
---
name: briefing/localisation-spec
owner: crea-paid-creative-copy
version: 1
invoke_when: creative or copy needs specifying for a target market and
  device with its own payment, delivery and language norms
inputs: brand brain market policies, device target
outputs: target spec sheet: device, trust facts, language notes, market tag
---
Purpose: fix the real, checkable local facts a creative or copy set must use,
so a market-specific ad never carries the wrong market's assumption by
accident.

Steps
1. Confirm the device target: the US default is standard feed and story
   formats; a market whose traffic skews mobile-first (for example an
   India-facing brief) defaults to vertical-only formats instead.
2. Pull the market's real trust facts from the brand brain: the payment
   method mix (card, Shop Pay, PayPal, Apple Pay, BNPL such as Affirm,
   Klarna or Afterpay for a US brand; COD availability and EMI where the
   target market runs them, markets: IN), the actual delivery window, and
   which local payment logos are true to show.
3. Note the language pair and whether the persona's real speech pattern
   calls for a dual-language, code-switched hook (for example a natural
   Hindi-English mix for an India-market brief) rather than a straight
   translation.
4. Flag any trust line inherited from a source market that does not hold
   here: a foreign-currency guarantee, a shipping time that does not apply,
   a payment method not actually offered.
5. Set the market tag that every downstream asset in this run must carry, so
   it can never be accidentally served to the wrong market.

Checks: every fact traces to current policy, not assumption; device target
stated.

Output: the target spec sheet, feeding the localisation workflow's copy and
resize steps.

Example, US brand: spec confirms the payment mix is card, Shop Pay and
Klarna, delivery is 3 to 5 business days, and any inherited COD or EMI line
is dropped since it does not apply. Example, India-market brief (markets:
IN): spec confirms COD is offered, EMI starts at a stated amount, and the
US "free returns within 30 days" line is replaced with the real local
return window.

name: Copy craft rules pass
invoke_when: any drafted copy needs the account's fixed direct-response writing rules applied before the claim-tier check
steps: Check reading level in code; simplify until it clears grade 10.
Check single-idea discipline: one dominant appeal, one CTA, per asset.
Rank proof points by strongest real evidence first.
Cut em dashes, inflated words and any AI-tell phrasing.
Confirm digits are used instead of spelled-out numbers.
checks: reading level under grade 10
one dominant appeal and one CTA held throughout
no em dash, no inflated word
output: edited copy with a reading-level score and an edit log
skill_md:
---
name: compliance/copy-craft-rules
owner: crea-paid-creative-copy
version: 1
invoke_when: any drafted copy needs the account's fixed writing rules applied,
  before the separate claim-tier check
inputs: draft copy
outputs: edited copy, reading-level score, edit log
---
Purpose: apply the same fixed craft rules to every draft regardless of which
skill wrote it, so voice and readability never drift by writer or by format.

Steps
1. Score reading level in code (not by eye) and rewrite until the draft
   clears the grade-10 target; a draft that reads clever but tests at grade
   13 gets simplified, not defended.
2. Check single-idea discipline: exactly one dominant appeal and exactly one
   CTA per asset, unless the approved idea explicitly calls for testing two
   in the same piece.
3. Order proof points from strongest real evidence to weakest, cutting any
   proof point with nothing behind it rather than padding the count.
4. Cut every em dash, every inflated or vague superlative with no fact
   behind it, and any phrasing that reads as generically AI-written rather
   than in the brand's real voice.
5. Replace spelled-out numbers with digits throughout.

Checks: grade-10 or below; single idea and single CTA; no em dash; digits,
not spelled-out numbers.

Output: the edited copy, its reading-grade score, and a short edit log
naming what changed and why.

Example: "we're absolutely thrilled to introduce an incredible new way to
elevate your morning" becomes "start your morning with 2 minutes of real
energy, no crash."

name: Rights clearance check
invoke_when: a video ad uses licensed stock footage, fonts or music, or a shoot needs signed releases, before anything ships
steps: List every licensed footage, font and music asset used, cross-checked against the actual timeline.
Pull each asset's real license terms: commercial use, territory, term length, exclusivity.
Match the video's actual use (paid ad, territory, campaign duration) to each license's real limits.
Swap or flag any mismatch before the asset ships.
Log the clearance with each license's expiry or renewal date.
checks: every asset in the final piece has a matching, logged license
no mismatched asset remains at ship time
output: license terms per asset, cleared asset set, clearance log entry
skill_md:
---
name: compliance/rights-clearance
owner: crea-paid-creative-copy
version: 1
invoke_when: a video uses licensed stock, fonts or music, or a shoot needs
  releases, before anything ships
inputs: finished asset with licensed elements, license documents or release
  forms
outputs: license terms per asset, cleared asset set, clearance log
---
Purpose: catch a license or release mismatch before an ad ships, since a
takedown or a rights claim on a live ad is far costlier than a swap caught at
this stage.

Steps
1. List every piece of stock footage, font and music track actually used in
   the finished timeline, checked against the real timeline, not remembered
   from the brief.
2. Pull each asset's real license document and read its actual terms:
   whether commercial use is covered, which territory, how long the term
   runs, and whether it is exclusive to this brand.
3. Match the video's real use, a paid ad, running in a specific territory,
   for a specific campaign duration, against each license's actual limits.
4. Where a mismatch turns up, swap the asset for a compliant one before the
   video ships; if no compliant replacement exists, this stops and the
   founder decides whether to reshoot, re-license or drop the asset.
5. Log the clearance for each asset with its expiry or renewal date, so a
   later renewal risk is tracked, not rediscovered by surprise.

Checks: every asset has a logged, matching license; no mismatch ships.

Output: the per-asset license terms, the cleared set, and a dated clearance
log entry.

Example: a background music track's license covers organic use only; it is
swapped for a paid-ad-licensed track before the video enters CREA-W01's
launch checklist.

invoke_when: a new AI tool or capability is entering the creative pipeline, or the standing AI-use policy needs a periodic check
inputs_required: new AI tool or capability description
steps: List every point AI drafts, generates or grades something in CREA's workflows.
Classify each as drafting/grunt work (allowed unsupervised) or final ideation/authorship (never unsupervised).
Confirm each drafting touchpoint is fed real brand facts, not generic training knowledge.
Classify and add any new tool to the policy before its first real use.
Publish and log the updated policy.
checks: no final-ideation touchpoint runs unsupervised
every AI draft grounded in a named brand-fact input
output: AI touchpoint map, classified list, updated policy
skill_md:
---
name: compliance/ai-use-governance
owner: crea-paid-creative-copy
version: 1
invoke_when: a new AI tool enters the pipeline, or the standing AI-use policy
  needs its periodic check
inputs: current AI-use policy, new AI tool or capability description
outputs: AI touchpoint map, classified list, updated policy
---
Purpose: keep a clear, current line between where AI may draft or automate
grunt work unsupervised and where a person must originate the idea or the
final call, across every workflow CREA runs.

Steps
1. List every point in CREA's workflows where AI drafts, generates, scores or
   grades something, from a headline draft to a predictive creative score.
2. Classify each: drafting or grunt work (readability scoring, resizing,
   tagging, first-pass variant generation) can run unsupervised; final
   ideation or unsupervised authorship (the angle itself, the founder's
   claims, a name) never can.
3. Confirm every drafting touchpoint is actually fed the brand's own facts,
   claim tiers, voice notes, product data, rather than defaulting to general
   knowledge with no brand grounding.
4. When a new AI capability arrives, an AI-actor generator, a voice clone
   tool, classify it under this same rule and add it to the policy before
   its first real use, never after.
5. Publish the current policy where every workflow can read it and log the
   update with a date.

Checks: no final-ideation step is unsupervised; every drafting step names
its brand-fact input.

Output: the touchpoint map and the current, dated AI-use policy.

Example: a new AI voice-clone tool is classified as drafting-only, gated
behind documented consent, and added to the policy before CREA-W20 uses it.

name: Naming and tagging standard
invoke_when: any asset needs a stable id and tags, or the platform-spec sheet or schema needs its periodic refresh
steps: Apply the fixed naming schema (campaign, ad-set, ad layers) to the asset.
Tag by concept, persona, angle, offer, format, stage, source.
Refresh the platform character-limit and spec sheet if it is over 30 days old.
Audit a sample of recent assets for schema drift and re-tag anything drifted.
Update the schema itself only for a genuinely new format, persona or offer type.
checks: every asset has a stable id
no platform-limit check older than 30 days when copy is being written to a limit
output: named, tagged asset; refreshed platform-spec sheet; updated schema when needed
skill_md:
---
name: production-ops/naming-and-tagging
owner: crea-paid-creative-copy
version: 1
invoke_when: any asset needs a stable id and tags, or the platform-spec sheet
  or schema is due its periodic refresh
inputs: asset metadata, current platform specs, current naming schema
outputs: named/tagged asset, refreshed spec sheet, updated schema when needed
---
Purpose: keep every asset findable by a fixed schema, and keep the platform
spec sheet current, since a copy set built to a stale character limit fails
silently on upload.

Steps
1. Apply the fixed naming schema across its layers, campaign, ad-set, ad, so
   any asset's id tells a person what it is without opening the file.
2. Tag every asset on all 7 fixed fields: concept, persona, angle, offer,
   format, stage and source; a missing tag is a stop, not a skip.
3. Check the platform character-limit and spec sheet's last-checked date; if
   it is over 30 days old, re-check it against the platform's current help
   documentation before any copy gets written to that limit.
4. Periodically audit a sample of recently shipped assets against the
   current schema, naming every instance of drift found, and re-tag them.
